source: Six learner attempts saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Affirmative command objects and command versus infinitive
summary: Correctly recalled prueba and informal lee, with esta función appropriate. Introduced object suffixes on affirmative tú commands. First review-it response used infinitive revisarla; tutor explained revísala. Then correctly formed revísalo, pruébala and léela, with accents supplied. Command morphology success assessed separately from orthography.

observations.outcome: Correct prueba after intervening material without a fresh stem hint; appropriate esta función. Función accent supplied. Same-day recall, no durable mastery claim.

Correct informal tú lee with register explicitly named, without a fresh conjugated model. Tutor then introduced affirmative-command pronoun attachment using lee + la → léela, with stress-preserving accent.

Target was Review it, please for la función. Learner used infinitive revisarla, meaning to review it; tutor supplied revisa + la → revísala and emphasized no r in this command. Infinitives can serve other directive functions in Spanish; do not infer a universal prohibition beyond the practised personal tú target.
Correct command base and masculine lo for stated el logo after feminine model. Only accent and conventional punctuation supplied; no infinitive r remained.
Correct prueba stem, suffix la and affirmative command construction without full target model. Accent supplied. Prompted transfer from review/read attachment examples.
Correct lee + la command after intervening commands, with léela earlier modelled at introduction. Accent supplied; retention beyond this immediate practice sequence untested.

nextSteps: Contrast Necesitamos revisarla with Revísala in separate meaning prompts
Recheck affirmative object-command forms after intervening material
Introduce negative commands only as a separate later unit
assessmentNote: Prompted production, prior models and supplied accents are explicit. No negative-command object placement or broad mastery inferred.
